evidence: rabbitmq-bridge.service.ts:~641-676 (origin/main) scopes the provider lookup with .eq(restaurant_id) whenever payload.restaurant_id is set (inbound-domain webhook stamps it, inbound-email.controller.ts:86-100). Only the Gmail push path (communications.controller.ts:~1288 publishes no restaurant_id) and a null-resolved inbound address fall to unscoped ilike+limit(1). Thread match (:~815-824) has no house filter and :~844 sets restaurantId = origin.restaurant_id || restaurantId; 2b guess (:~859-877) can also overwrite. A mixed row needs the same vendor email in providers of 2+ houses (plus ilike treats _ and % in the address as wildcards). PR #681 is OPEN, unmerged.
corrected_claim: On the shared-Gmail path (and inbound-domain mail with no resolved house), a vendor email present in providers of more than one house is matched by an unscoped ilike limit(1); the thread and newest-open-order steps can then set restaurant_id from a different house than provider_id. Not a general misfile: the dedicated-domain path is already house-scoped. Blocker only once a second house shares a vendor email; production has one real tenant, so major.

evidence: Confirmed for shared-mailbox Gmail push: gmail-watch.service.ts:185-230 fetchNewMessages calls history.list with no pageToken, stores the new historyId (updateHistoryId, 7-day TTL 604800 at :~179) before the controller publishes; 404 branch calls startWatch and returns [] (gap dropped); communications.controller.ts:~1309-1313 catches publish errors and only logs. Bridge acks before the un-awaited handler and queue has x-message-ttl 300000 / x-max-length 1000 (rabbitmq-bridge.service.ts:~358-380); insert error only logs. inbound-email.controller.ts returns HTTP 200 for every outcome (even bad secret/error), no retry. NOT true of the house reader: house-inbox.service.ts uses a durable house_inbox_cursors row and re-reads on failure (:~521, :~547-567) driven by house-inbox.cron.ts @Cron. Only manual recovery exists for push: POST webhooks/gmail/force-fetch.
corrected_claim: Mail can be lost silently on the shared-mailbox Gmail push path and the inbound-parse webhook (cursor advanced before publish, unpaginated history, swallowed publish error, 200 on every outcome), and on every path at the bridge (ack before handler, 5-min TTL, 1000 cap, failed insert only logged). The personal-mailbox house reader has a durable cursor and a cron re-read. No automatic fallback poll exists for the shared mailbox; only the manual force-fetch.

evidence: procurement.service.ts:8389-8432 sendProviderEmail calls gmailService.sendEmail with no fromName; gmail.service.ts:730 defaults fromName to 'Mudavym' and :741 uses this.senderEmail (deployment mailbox). Callers at :7936, :8671, :8958, :9833 confirmed. HouseSenderService is wired only via communications.module and house-letters.controller; recommendation-digest.service.ts:114 explicitly does not use it. ADR 0118 D1 (decisions/0118...md:130-160) is worded about a 'letter' leaving from the house's mailbox, never from the deployment's shared mailbox; it does not name the procurement order/negotiation sendProviderEmail path, which is the legacy path.
corrected_claim: Order and negotiation mail sent by procurement.service.ts sendProviderEmail leaves from the deployment mailbox as 'Mudavym' (Reply-To is only a per-house inbound address when INBOUND_EMAIL_DOMAIN is set). ADR 0118 D1 governs house letters; whether it also binds this older path is a reading, not stated in D1.

evidence: rabbitmq-bridge.service.ts:~680-762: no provider match -> only outreach-looking mail (attachment or promotional, non-bulk) becomes a Prospect; otherwise logger.warn 'no provider found ... (not leaded)' and return (:~757-764). ADR 0118 D9 bounds the house reader by the vendor book. ADR 0118 :214 states procurement_conversations.provider_id is NOT NULL.

useCommsNextData.ts:122 reads useProcurementConversationHistory -> GET procurement/conversations/history, which is .limit(100) ordered created_at desc, restaurant-scoped, with the draft/pending/house-letter exclusions (procurement.service.ts:10329; the cited :4208 is wrong on origin/main). The page also reads useActiveConversations for drafts. Deep links: CommunicationsNext.tsx:420,440 reads ?draft and ?reply (reply=orderId, :460) and WhoIsWriting.tsx:416 reads ?senders; there is no thread-id or message-id link. useConversationThreads is imported only by useSortingOfficeData.ts:37,185.
corrected_claim: The /communications book is the newest 100 vendor-linked rows, flat, not threaded; its only deep links are ?draft=<id> and ?reply=<orderId> (an order, not a thread or message). The threaded endpoint is used only by the documents Sorting Office page.

evidence: raw-mail-retention.service.ts:547-551 sweepHouse reads procurement_conversations filtered .not('mirrored_by_grant_id','is',null); sweepForRevokedGrant :649-651 filters eq grant id. The bridge sets mirrored_by_grant_id null for shared mailbox and inbound-domain (rabbitmq-bridge.service.ts:~663-666). ADR 0118 D12 deliberately defines the window for 'a copy of somebody's mailbox' (a person's grant). No retention code for prospect bodies found (grep over apps/api-gateway/src and supabase/migrations). Attachment bytes deleted only through the same sweeps (:777).
corrected_claim: The retention window and revocation purge cover only mail mirrored from a person's mailbox grant, by design in D12/D15. Raw mail and attachments from the shared mailbox and inbound domain, and prospect bodies, have no sweep; whether that is a gap or intended is not stated in D12-D15. 'Forever' is the absence of any deletion code, not a stated policy.

evidence: communications.controller.ts:76 class guard is JwtAuthGuard only; forceGmailFetch (:~1345-1462) has no @Roles, no restaurant check, lists the shared INBOX for minutesBack (body, default 60) and republishes with gmail_message_id set, so the bridge dedupe (:~885-898) skips already stored mail. Comment says it is left reachable on purpose. useForceFetchReplies (useDraftEmailQueries.ts:575) has no caller on origin/main (grep of apps/web/src).
corrected_claim: Any signed-in member of any house can trigger a replay of the shared mailbox's last N minutes (caller-chosen, default 60) with no role or house scope; replays are idempotent via gmail_message_id dedupe, and no UI button calls it. Not a replay of the whole inbox.

evidence: inbound-email.controller.ts:~50-75 accepts x-inbound-secret header or ?secret= query and compares with !== ; publishes gmail_message_id: null, gmail_thread_id: null so the bridge dedupe (:~885, only if gmailMessageId) never applies. INBOUND_EMAIL_DOMAIN/PROVIDER/WEBHOOK_SECRET are absent from env.example and services/agent-orchestrator/.env.example but present in .railway/railway.ts:121-123. addressFor is used at procurement.service.ts:8414 (Reply-To) and also menus.controller.ts:289 (menu intake address), so one house screen may show an address for menus, not mail.
corrected_claim: The inbound-parse webhook accepts the secret in the query string, compares non-constant-time, and has no dedupe (no gmail_message_id; Message-ID header is not used as a key). The env vars are declared in railway.ts but missing from env.example. No mail screen shows the house its inbound address; it is shown only for menu intake.

evidence: conversations.service.ts:827-852 getStats selects id,channel,direction,provider_id,detected_sentiment,created_at for every row of the house with no limit/range and aggregates in JS (also subject to PostgREST's row cap). listConversationThreads :572-660 is paged by thread via the list_conversation_threads RPC (p_limit/p_offset), then fetches all messages of only that page's thread keys with select * plus providers and procurement_orders joins. The claim that ADR 0357/PR #747 depends on it was not verified.
corrected_claim: getStats is an unbounded per-house read aggregated in JS. The thread list is paged by thread; the over-fetch is select * (full bodies and headers) for every message of each paged thread, not an unbounded read.

evidence: conversations.service.ts:~800 publishes email.summarize.requested; grep of services/ finds no subscriber or handler for it. publishEvent (:306-330) POSTs ${AGENT_ORCHESTRATOR_URL}/api/v1/events/publish; grep of services/agent-orchestrator finds no such route, and the code comment itself describes a PERMANENT 404/405 case. AGENT_ORCHESTRATOR_URL is set in .railway/railway.ts:105. useRegenerateSummary (useConversationQueries.ts:243) has no caller. Production behavior was not checked (no prod access).
corrected_claim: On origin/main, Regenerate summary has no subscriber and its HTTP publish targets a route that the orchestrator source does not define; it throws rather than silently succeeding, and no UI calls it. 'Unreachable in production' is not verified, only absent in source.

evidence: house-sender.service.ts:~383-385: chosen = withSend.find(r => String(r.user_id) === userId) ?? withSend[0]; the file has no .order( call. So the asking person's own send grant wins; nondeterminism applies only when they have none and 2+ others exist. A null account_email is handled explicitly (:~392+ words name the person instead of an address).
corrected_claim: When several members hold send grants, the asker's own grant is preferred; only the fallback to withSend[0] has no ORDER BY. A null address is expected for gmail_send and is handled with a truthful sentence.

evidence: communications.controller.ts:127-160 sender-identity returns scope 'deployment' and perHouse.supported:false with a reason saying no per-restaurant sender exists, while house-letters.controller.ts:59-80 GET letters/sender resolves a per-house identity via HouseSenderService.resolve. useConnectionsNextData.ts:585-607 reads sender-identity as 'the address the letters leave from' and letters/sender only for the receive-half reader status ('Separate ... on purpose'), so Settings does not show both answers for the same question.
corrected_claim: The two endpoints disagree about who sends for the house (sender-identity is stale: it says per-house is unsupported), and Settings uses sender-identity for the send address, so it can show the deployment address while letters/sender would resolve a house mailbox. Settings reads letters/sender only for reader status.

evidence: gmail.service.ts:~276-280 threadId is set on the API branch only; the SMTP branch (taken only when ensureGmailReady() fails, :~250-262) sets messageId (options.messageIdHeader), inReplyTo and references (:~849-852) and returns no threadId. Message-ID is minted as <mudavym-uuid@wineops.ai> (procurement.service.ts:8385-8386) and the default generated id is @wineops.ai (gmail.service.ts:733). The bridge's thread match needs a stored outbound row with gmail_thread_id; SMTP results carry none, so such replies may fall to the 2b order guess.
corrected_claim: On the SMTP fallback (used only when Gmail API init fails), the result has no gmail threadId so the stored outbound row cannot anchor a thread match, though Message-ID, In-Reply-To and References headers are set. The @wineops.ai Message-ID domain is true but unrelated to threading.

evidence: house-inbox.cron.ts:38 private last: InboxReadRun | null, lastRun() :42, header comment :23 says it is null until the first tick, never a fabricated 'nothing to do'. Served by house-letters.controller.ts senderIdentity (dispatcher/reader). Whether production runs more than one gateway instance was not checked.
corrected_claim: lastRun() is per-instance memory; on an instance that has not ticked it returns null, which the contract treats as 'has not run', not as 'read nothing'. Impact depends on multi-instance deployment (unverified).

evidence: rabbitmq-bridge.service.ts:~985-989 new-mail notice action_url is /orders?order=<id> or undefined; prospect notices use actionUrl '/communications' with no anchor (:~745,755). RecurringOrders.tsx:~141 window.location.assign('/communications'), but its comment says the page has no route in App.tsx (orphaned), so it is not a live entry point. ProviderConversationMemory is rendered by ProviderIntelligencePanel.tsx:120 and reads its own memory store (fetchConversationMemory).
corrected_claim: The new-mail notice lands on an order or nowhere, prospect notices land on /communications unanchored, and the provider panel shows a separate memory store. The RecurringOrders reload is in an orphaned page and should be dropped from the claim.

evidence: On origin/main grep of apps/web/src (excluding tests) finds no caller of useConversations, useConversationThread, useConversationStats, useRegenerateSummary or useForceFetchReplies, and no import of ConversationApprovalNotification. useConversationQueries.ts:1-20 builds its own axios instance reading accessToken and activeRestaurantId from localStorage; that instance is live because useProcurementConversationHistory (:333) uses it.
